items.headline: Blue Origin expands Florida site to launch up to 150 New Glenn rockets annually
items.title: Blue Origin is going all in on the New Glenn rocket
items.scifi_hook: Blue Origin plans new pads, a massive upper‑stage factory, and extra landing ships to boost New Glenn launch cadence.
items.eli5: Blue Origin will build more launch pads, a factory for rocket parts, and ships to catch returning boosters at its Florida base.
items.why: Higher launch capacity could reshape commercial heavy‑lift market.
items.text: Blue Origin announced a major expansion of its already considerable Florida launch facilities on Friday morning with the intent of eventually flying 150 rockets a year from there. The company said it would add two additional launch pads for the New Glenn rocket, in addition to two already under construction at Cape Canaveral. The company is also investing heavily in a new manufacturing facility that will produce up to 150 upper stages for a larger variant of the New Glenn rocket. Additionally, the company plans to procure two additional landing ships to catch and return the first stage of the New Glenn rocket (it currently has one, named Jacklyn ). Finally, Blue Origin said it would add a new customer integration facility, built in conjunction with the US Space Force, that will feature four payload bays to process multiple missions at the same time. items.headline: Tech firms eye equity stakes in Anglo American amid copper shortage
items.title: Tech giants come knocking for a piece of Anglo American as copper scarcity bites, Wanblad tells  FT
items.scifi_hook: Silicon‑valley giants may buy shares in a copper miner to lock down the metal that powers data centres.
items.eli5: Tech companies are considering buying part of Anglo American to secure copper needed for servers.
items.why: Equity interest could drive demand and support copper prices.
items.text: Anglo American (LON: AAL) has held talks with technology companies interested in buying equity in the miner as a way of securing supplies of the metals that go into data centres, chief executive Duncan Wanblad told the Financial Times’ Metals and Mining Summit in London on Thursday. Discussions were “absolutely being had”, Wanblad said, with the question from the tech side coming down to whether to lock in long-term offtake directly or take an equity position to secure a stake in future supply. No stakes have been taken, but there had been “deep expressions of interest” in doing so, he told the summit. “Given the scarcity issue that we’ve been speaking about, a lot of people are looking for ways to secure supply.” Comex copper for December delivery traded near $6.52 a pound (about $14,370 a tonne) on Thursday, a third straight decline, after stronger than expected US inflation data put a Federal Reserve rate hike this month back on the table. Cash copper on the LME settled at a record $14,822 on Monday and the most-active Comex contract remains within 6% of its September 9 record settlement of $6.89. A $90 billion copper company Anglo’s New York-listed shares added 0.6% to $26.86 in early trade on Thursday for a market value of $58.0 billion, while Teck Resources (NYSE: TECK) edged up 0.3% to $64.96 and is worth $31.9 billion. items.headline: US announces $3 billion for mining and mineral processing, plus $250 billion infrastructure plan
items.title: Op-Ed: New investment could reshape US mining
items.scifi_hook: Washington pledges billions to revive domestic mines and train the next generation of mineral engineers.
items.eli5: The US government is spending billions to fund new mines, processing plants, and mining education.
items.why: Funding aims to reduce reliance on foreign critical minerals.
items.text: Recent announcements suggest the United States may be entering a new period for domestic mining. The federal government has announced about $3 billion in investments for mining and mineral processing, including more than $180 million for education and workforce development . Bank of America has also announced a $250 billion infrastructure financing initiative that includes mining and critical minerals. For an industry accustomed to seeing projects struggle to secure financing and advance through permitting and processing, the scale of these commitments matters. Capital can help projects move forward, expand domestic capacity and address supply-chain vulnerabilities built up over decades. But mines take years to develop, and the people needed to design, build and operate them take years to train. Those timelines must be considered together. Enrollment figures show the size of the challenge. Enrollment in US mining engineering programs fell from nearly 1,500 students eight years ago to fewer than 600 in 2023, according to data compiled by the Society for Mining, Metallurgy & Exploration (SME) and the Society of Mining Professors. Anecdotal evidence suggests the numbers may be improving, but demand for minerals used in energy, manufacturing, infrastructure and national security continues to grow. items.headline: Terra Quantum joins QuEra Alliance to link software with neutral‑atom hardware
items.title: Terra Quantum Joins QuEra Quantum Alliance
items.scifi_hook: A software firm plugs its cloud quantum platform into a future fault‑tolerant atom computer.
items.eli5: Terra Quantum adds its cloud‑based quantum code tools to work with QuEra's atom‑based quantum machines.
items.why: It could speed up enterprise use of next‑gen quantum computers.
items.text: Insider Brief Terra Quantum has joined the QuEra Quantum Alliance, adding its quantum software, algorithms and enterprise application expertise to the neutral-atom quantum computing partner network. Terra Quantum ‘s TQ42 platform provides a cloud-based quantum software environment with a Python SDK, APIs and algorithms for optimization, quantum machine learning and simulation. The partnership aims to connect enterprise applications with QuEra’s neutral-atom hardware, as QuEra targets availability of its 256-logical-qubit Libra fault-tolerant quantum computer through Amazon Braket in 2028. PRESS RELEASE — Terra Quantum , a global leader in the development of quantum technologies and their industrial application, the leader in neutral-atom quantum computing, today announced that Terra Quantum has joined the QuEra Quantum Alliance, a global partner program dedicated to accelerating the development, deployment, and utilization of neutral-atom quantum computers to solve the world’s most challenging computational problems. Reinforcing the Applications Layer of the QuEra Quantum Alliance Terra Quantum is hardware-agnostic by design, developing proprietary algorithms and software rather than quantum processors.
